nodes.title: start-secuura.sh and start-local.sh print the demo issuer password in their startup banners
nodes.description:
## BLUF

**Two platform-k start scripts print a password in clear on every successful start.** Both echo the demo issuer account's email *and its password* in their closing "Credentials" banner:

| Script | Line (`develop` `0f2422925`) | Last change |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` | `:711`, `echo -e "    Issuer:  demo@secuura.io / <password>"` | `7b14f84ff`, 2026-09-22 |
| `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/start-local.sh` | `:251`, `echo "    Issuer:  demo@secuura.io  / <password>"` | `48641bda3`, 2026-09-05 |

The value is not reproduced here. The banner goes to the terminal, and from there into anything that captures stdout: CI logs, `nohup` / background-run logs (it is in this session's `$TMPDIR` start log), pasted bug reports and screenshots.

The platform-s rule (platform-s `CLAUDE.md` → *Security Considerations*) is: *"platform-k: a script or service there that prints or logs a password is raised as a **Critical** defect, assigned to Kamil."* That is why this is raised Urgent and assigned to you.

## Measured (5 Oct 2026)

* **The printed credential is live.** The same script's own login check (`start-secuura.sh:603`, which uses the same literal in a `curl` body) logged `Issuer login (demo@secuura.io)` as a success on a fresh K slot 3 (`46c3e20cf`, `--rebuild --fresh-db`).
* **Re-verified on the current** `origin/develop` `0f2422925`**:** both lines are still present, and no other `*.sh` under the repo echoes the literal.

## Severity context (stated so it can be weighed, not used to wave it through)

* This is the **published demo sample login**: platform-k `CLAUDE.md:107` names it, and [KS-668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-668/compose-seeds-published-123-credentials-by-default-and-the-11-rotation)'s scope note calls the demo logins deliberate, documented sample credentials. So the secret itself is already public.
* What the banner adds: it makes a known-default credential the thing every operator reads at the end of every start, on **every** compose deploy that runs these scripts. [KS-668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-668/compose-seeds-published-123-credentials-by-default-and-the-11-rotation) shows the same compose path seeds these defaults by default (`ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` defaults to `true`), and that rotating them through `.env` is silently ignored. So on a box where an operator *thinks* they rotated it, the banner still prints the old value, and the old value may still work.
* It also undercuts the "never print a password" rule both platforms hold. A script that prints one is the precedent the next script copies.

## Not covered by existing tickets (checked)

* [KS-972](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-972/start-secuurash-banner-prints-adminsecuuracom-admin123-which-has) (In Progress, PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1180](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-972-banner-start-secuurash-no-longer-prints-the-retired-admin-850ff68f818a)) fixed the **Admin** half of the same banner and explicitly left the Issuer half: *"the issuer half is correct and only the admin half is stale."* Its concern was a stale credential, not a printed one. It wasn't updated here because it is In Progress.
* [KS-668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-668/compose-seeds-published-123-credentials-by-default-and-the-11-rotation) (Backlog) covers compose seeding of the `*123` defaults and the broken rotation channel, not scripts printing them.
* [KS-951](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-951/the-default-password-ci-gate-catches-one-shape-and-calls-it-clean-16) (Backlog) covers the default-password CI lint. That lint scans only `.ts/.tsx/.js` under `services/` and `packages/`, so it cannot see a `.sh` banner. That's why nothing has flagged these lines.
* [KS-966](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-966/retire-the-published-system-admin-credential-kam-rotate-properly-a) retired the published SYSTEM_ADMIN credential. Its item 3 covers scripts that *read* a fallback, not scripts that *print* one.

## Suggested fix (your call)

1. Print the mechanism, not the value, as [KS-972](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-972/start-secuurash-banner-prints-adminsecuuracom-admin123-which-has) did for the admin line. For example: `Issuer: demo@secuura.io (password: DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD, or the published demo default; see CLAUDE.md)`.
2. Make `start-secuura.sh:603`'s login check read the password from the environment instead of a literal, so the script doesn't carry the value at all.
3. Extend the [KS-951](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-951/the-default-password-ci-gate-catches-one-shape-and-calls-it-clean-16) gate, or add a small `.sh` check, so a script that echoes a known seeded password fails the gate.

## Acceptance

* Neither banner prints a password value. A stack start's captured stdout contains no seeded password.
* A guard fails if a `.sh` under `Start_Up/` or `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/` echoes one.

---

*Found 5 Oct 2026 while bringing up K slot 3 for platform-s* [PS-1003](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1003/verification-policies-leaves-a-deployment-wide-block-policy-which) *(*`up-slot.sh 3`*). No K code was changed.
